# Troubleshooting ABS/ESP Lights on a Peugeot 308 After Brake Disc Replacement

If you recently replaced rear brake discs on a 2010 Peugeot 308 and immediately encountered illuminated ABS and ESP fault lights, the issue likely stems from how the new hardware interacts with the existing wheel speed sensors. The diagnostic trouble code (DTC) `C1326` indicates that a test is currently inhibited by another active fault stored in non-volatile memory. This specific status means the control module has detected a primary error and disabled further self-checks to prevent false positives or unsafe operation until the root cause is resolved. The absence of this code in standard generic Peugeot lists suggests it is a manufacturer-specific internal flag rather than a universal OBD-II standard, which often confuses independent mechanics who rely on third-party scanners.

When fitting new discs, rust buildup around the wheel hub is a common culprit. If this corrosion was not thoroughly cleaned before mounting the sensors, the sensor tip may not sit flush against the reluctor ring or the housing. Even a microscopic gap can disrupt the magnetic field required for accurate wheel speed detection. While continuity checks on the hall-effect or reactive sensors showed approximately 460 Ohms on both sidesâwhich is generally within acceptable tolerance rangesâresistance alone does not guarantee signal integrity. The physical alignment between the sensor and the rotating reluctor ring is critical.

A significant indicator that the system is still functional despite the warning lights is the behavior of cruise control and the speedometer. On many architectures, including this Peugeot 308, the ESP module relies on wheel speed data for stability control interventions but does not disable standard instrumentation or cruise functions if a single wheel sensor is marginal or if the ABS pump is inhibited. The fact that these features remain operational suggests the vehicle can still transmit speed data to the ECU, even if the specific ABS modulation algorithm cannot validate the signal with full confidence. This distinction is vital for safety: the car will not engage braking assistance during hard stops, but it will continue to drive under normal conditions.

The breakthrough in this diagnosis comes from observing the raw sensor output. Using a multimeter set to capture the AC voltage or frequency of the ABS sensor allows you to visualize the waveform. In a healthy scenario, the signal should be a clean sine wave whose amplitude increases proportionally with wheel speed. If the flat portions of the waveform persist even when the wheel is spinning, it indicates a break in the magnetic circuit caused by damage to the reluctor ring. Rust removal or improper disc installation can chip the teeth on this ring, creating a gap that the sensor cannot bridge consistently.

To resolve `C1326`, you must first clear the stored fault code using the diagnostic tool to reset the "test inhibited" status. However, if the primary error remainsâspecifically damage to the reluctor ringâthe light will return immediately upon driving. If visual inspection of the wheel hub confirms the ring is intact and the sensor gap is less than 1mm after cleaning all rust from the mating surfaces, a sensor replacement may be warranted. The trade-off here is cost versus diagnostic time; replacing both rear sensors is often cheaper than investigating ABS pump issues, but it is unnecessary if the reluctor ring itself is compromised. Always verify the physical integrity of the rotating assembly before concluding that the electronic components are at fault.
